question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the following sentence.

He made the business profitable from unprofitable in about a year of joining.

options.text: Where there is a will, there is a way

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **"Where there is a will, there is a way"** means if someone is determined to do something, they will find a way to accomplish it, despite obstacles. (जहाँ चाह वहाँ राह)

 
 
• **Example:** Despite numerous difficulties, she completed her education because she firmly believed that **where there is a will, there is a way.**
 
 

Therefore, the most appropriate idiom for the given sentence is **'Where there is a will, there is a way'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Easy come, easy go** (आसानी से आया, आसानी से गया): Something that is easily gained or achieved is also easily lost.

 
 
• **Example:** He won a lot of money in the lottery but lost it all in a year.** Easy come, easy go.**
 
 
 
• **Throw up** (उल्टी करना): To vomit.
 
 
• **Example:** He felt so sick that he had to** throw up.**
 
 
 
• **Still waters run deep** (शांत पानी गहरा होता है): A quiet or placid manner may conceal a passionate nature.
 
 
• **Example:** She might seem calm, but **still waters run deep.**
